title: Stop two transfers from spending the same credits

blocks.text: This practice continues the `Wallets` of the previous one: `publish()` and `balances()` are done, and `transfer(...)` is now yours to write.

Players send each other credits in bursts, and the owner thread is often still busy with one transfer when the next ones are requested. Finance found two wallets below zero last month: each had been the source of two transfers requested within a few milliseconds, either of which it could cover alone.

Write `transfer(from, to, credits)` in `src/main/java/practice/Wallets.java`. It returns at once with a `Future` that says whether the transfer went through. A wallet never goes below zero, and a transfer requested while an earlier one is still being applied sees that earlier one's result: credits it brings in can be spent, credits it takes out can't. About eight lines in total.
The tests pause a transfer half-way through `Seam.midTransfer()`, so call it between taking the credits and adding them.

cases.says: transfers one after another move credits, and a transfer the wallet can't cover is refused
two transfers requested while another is in progress, each covered by the wallet alone but not together, are not both applied
a transfer requested while an earlier one is still adding credits to its wallet can spend those credits

origin.section: One Lock Makes the Total Right; One Owner Thread Also Keeps Readers From Waiting

concepts: A decision about owned state is made inside the owner's task; a check on a snapshot followed by a submitted change is a check-then-act that lets two callers pass.
